The '''1973–74 season''' was '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|71st season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|42nd consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football.

==Summary==
During the summer, the Spanish Football Federation lifted the ban on the transfers of foreign players after eleven seasons.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2020/05/26/reportajes/1590459438_017479.html|publisher=as.com|title=A League of Foreigners|language=Spanish|author=Ignacio Camacho|access-date=1 July 2020}}</ref> As such, Madrid signed Argentine forward [[Oscar Más]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/2003/10/28/polideportivo/1067318207_850215.html|publisher=as.com|title=Pinino Mas The leftist with an Electrifying Volley|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref> German midfielder [[Günter Netzer]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2014/07/17/primera/1405560847_317159.html|publisher=as.com|date=17 July 2014|access-date=2 July 2020|title=9 German Players in Real Madrid}}</ref> as well as bringing in Spanish teenage defender [[José Antonio Camacho]] and youngster [[Vicente del Bosque]]. On 8 September 1973, the club announced plans to build a new stadium in [[Fuencarral]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2015/02/15/actualidad/1424026392_562172.html|publisher=elpais.com|title=Bernabeu Wanted to Take Down The Bernabeu|date=24 April 2013|accessdate=31 August 2021|language=Spanish}}</ref> a project that was ultimately rejected by City Government.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2016/10/17/5805120b22601dcf608b45bd.html|title=The Lost Stadium of Real Madrid|publisher=marca.com|author=Alfredo Relaño|date=20 February 2014|accessdate=31 August 2021}}</ref> Madrid finished in just eighth place in the league table, sixteen points behind champions [[FC Barcelona|CF Barcelona]] and their new arrival, Dutch playmaker [[Johan Cruijff]], known internationally as Johan Cruyff.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spanhist6979.html|website=[[RSSSF]]|title= La Liga 1973-74}}</ref> Cruyff was instrumental in the 5–0 defeat of ''Los Blancos'' at the Bernabéu in the league Clásico.<ref>{{cite web|title=THE BEAUTY AND THE BRUTALITY OF THE DAY JOHAN CRUYFF LED BARCELONA TO A 5-0 WIN AT THE BERNABÉU|url=https://thesefootballtimes.co/2018/11/30/the-beauty-and-the-brutality-of-the-day-johan-cruyff-led-barcelona-to-a-5-0-win-at-the-bernabeu/}}</ref> During the campaign, [[Miguel Muñoz]] (head coach since 1960) was fired on 14 January 1974 after a bad streak of results, being replaced by [[Luis Molowny]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2020-04-26/del-milagro-miguel-munoz-al-fuera-munoz.html|title=From 'Miracle' Muñoz To Get Out Muñoz|publisher=El Pais|access-date= 2 July 2020|date=26 April 2020|language=Spanish|author=Alfredo Relaño}}</ref>

Meanwhile, in June the team won the [[1974 Copa del Generalísimo Final]] 4–0 against champions Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cadenaser.com/programa/2011/04/18/carrusel_deportivo/1303082892_850215.html|title=Madrid Takes Revenge In 1974 Copa del Generalisimo Final|publisher=Cadena SER|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref>

Shockingly, in the [[1973-74 UEFA Cup|UEFA Cup]] the squad bowed out early at the hands of [[Ipswich Town]] after losing the first leg of the series 0–1 and a achieving only a miserable draw 1–1 in Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.twtd.co.uk/blogs/21836/fiesta-time-as-town-bid-adios-to-real|publisher=TWTD.co.uk|title=Fiesta Time as Town Bid Adios to Real|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref>
